mechanism_narrative: Rising consumer demand, measured by HOUST, leads to higher corporate earnings expectations and thus a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not statistically different from zero when HOUST growth exceeds +2% in the preceding month (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A surge in employment, proxied by PAYEMS, reduces labor market uncertainty and boosts investor confidence, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window following a PAYEMS increase of >5% from the prior month, SPX 60-day returns are negative with p < 0.05 (two-tailed).

mechanism_narrative: A contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) suggests weakening supply-side momentum, which typically precedes a positive S&P 500 forward return as market participants anticipate potential rate cuts.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative when INDPRO declines by >-3% over the prior two months (rolling mean).

mechanism_narrative: When the Unemployment Rate (UNRATE) falls below 3.5%, it indicates labor market resilience that typically coincides with a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return as Fed rate-cut expectations rise.
failure_condition: UNRATE remains above 3.5% for 4 consecutive months with SPX 5-day returns all negative.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) suggest accelerating inflation expectations, which can trigger a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as the market anticipates a rate hike.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL does not show a 3-month upward trend for 6 months, and SPX 20-day returns remain non-negative.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the number of people file new job applications (PAYEMS) signals labor market strength that can drive a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return through optimism about economic expansion.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >15% in a single month
failure_condition: PAYEMS does not show a >15% monthly increase for 3 consecutive months, and SPX 60-day returns are flat or negative.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and a rise in consumer spending (HOUST) creates a demand-supply mismatch that predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as market participants anticipate supportive policy responses.
failure_condition: Over 20 days following such an interaction, SPX returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS > 4.5%), S&P 500 forward returns tend to be negative over the next 20 days as investors anticipate higher rates and reduced risk appetite.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS remains ≤ 4.5% for 6 consecutive months with all 20-day SPX returns non-negative.
